note: The four dreidel letters, what each stands for in the phrase and in the game, and the house rules Aleph plays by. Letter names follow data/letters/letters.json (letter ids play the existing letter clips). Words of the phrase are data/vocab/words.json entries.

hey.name: Hey
hey.ruleEn: Take half the pot. With an odd pot, round up.

shin.name: Shin
shin.ruleEn: Put one piece into the pot.

pe.name: Pe
pe.ruleEn: Put one piece into the pot (the same as Shin).

israelNote: In Israel the dreidel (סְבִיבוֹן, sevivon) has פ (Pe) instead of ש (Shin): פֹּה, po, means "here", because the miracle happened in the Land of Israel.
houseRules: Everyone starts with the same number of gelt pieces and puts one in the pot.
Take turns spinning. The letter that lands face up says what to do.
Hey with an odd pot: round up. A pot of 5 gives 3.
When the pot is empty or has one piece, everyone puts one in again.
A player with no gelt left is out. The last player with gelt wins; in a short game, the most gelt wins.
